hero.heading: What this component does
hero.description: A horizontal track that fills to show how far an ongoing process has got. Progress is a single value that grows from empty to full, with two further modes for when the extent is not known. An optional label above the bar reports the state in words. Nothing here animates, so both the fill's growth and the indeterminate movement belong to the implementation.

rows.Description: The bar reports one value that grows from empty to full. Figma offers it as four fixed steps only because a variant cannot hold a number, so pick the nearest when laying out and let the implementation drive the real value. The steps are samples, not thresholds worth designing around.
Work is happening but its extent is unknown. The indicator becomes a short segment that a real implementation slides along the track, so it should never sit still in a shipped screen.

Work is happening and part of the span ahead is already secured, as when a stream loads in advance. It adds a third band between the indicator and the track, and is the only value that changes the bar's anatomy.
Softened ends on both the track and the fill, matching the system's rounded controls.
Square ends, for a bar sitting flush against square surfaces. Beside rounded controls the two treatments read as different components.
The everyday bar, thin enough to sit under a label without dominating it.
A heavier bar for when progress is the main thing on the surface rather than a detail beside other content.
Shows the text row above the bar. The wording is fixed by the Progress value rather than set as a property, so it changes when the value does.
Hides the row, leaving the bar alone. Only do this where nearby copy already names the task, because a bar on its own reports a proportion and not a subject.
Shows the unfilled remainder behind the indicator, which is what makes the proportion readable.
Hides it, leaving only the filled portion. The bar then shows a length with nothing to measure it against.
No trailing content in the label row.
Reveals a slot at the trailing end of the label row for supporting detail. It shares the row with the label, so a long label and a filled slot will compete for the same space.

rows.What changes: The bar has no hover, pressed, focus or disabled states. It reports a value rather than accepting input, so the only thing that changes its appearance is the Progress value itself.
The indicator becomes a short fixed-length segment rather than a measured fill. Figma draws it in one position, a real implementation moves it along the track.
The same short indicator, plus a translucent band covering the buffered span between it and the end of the track.

rows.Description: Figma stores no timing and the bar models no transition. Every Progress value is a static snapshot, so the fill growing, and the indeterminate segment travelling, both belong to the implementation.
Both are drawn frozen in a single position. Shipping either as a still misrepresents them, because their whole meaning is that they are moving.
Width is fixed and height comes from the chosen Size, so the bar never grows with its content. A long label wraps inside the row above rather than widening the bar.

The row above the bar. It is not a text property, so its wording is fixed by the Progress value and has to be overridden on the instance to say anything else. The shipped strings read as placeholders, for example Uploading... on Indeterminate.

Trailing content in the label row, revealed by Show More Details. It ships holding a hidden Icon and suggests no components, so it stays empty until filled. One property serves every variant, so content placed here survives a change of Progress, Shape or Size.
Neither is a slot. The indicator's width is the value, so in Figma it is set by choosing the nearest step or overriding the width directly, and at runtime it is driven straight from the real number.

sections.title: Anatomy
rawTextContent: The outer frame. Fixed width, stacking the label row above the indicator group with a gap between them, and hugging whatever height the chosen Size produces.
Holds the text that reports the state and, when Show More Details is on, a trailing slot beside it.
The track, the indicator that fills it, and on Buffering a third band covering the buffered span.

sections.title: How to use
dos: Use Indeterminate or Buffering when the duration genuinely is not known. A measured bar sitting at a guessed percentage is worse than one that admits it cannot measure.
Keep the label on unless nearby copy already names what is progressing. The bar reports a proportion, not a subject.
donts: Don't ship Indeterminate or Buffering as a still. Both are drawn frozen here and only make sense in motion.
Don't leave the shipped label copy in place. Strings like Uploading... are placeholders tied to the variant, not wording anyone chose for your screen.

sections.title: Accessibility & Content Guidelines
items: The bar reports a value visually and nothing else. The current value, its range and what it refers to all have to be exposed in code.
The label wording is fixed per Progress value and the shipped strings read as placeholders. Replace them with copy that names the actual task.
Turning Show Track off removes the reference the fill is measured against, which makes the proportion much harder to judge.
Indeterminate and Buffering convey that work continues through movement. Someone who cannot perceive the animation gets no signal from them, so pair either with text.
The fill and the track are separated by colour alone. Check foreground/link against border/subtle on the surface you place the bar on.

rows.Description: 408px as drawn. The bar does not hug its content, so whoever places it decides the width.
44px at small and 52px at medium with the label shown. The difference is the indicator group, which is 8px at small and 16px at medium.
16px (space/lg) between the label row and the indicator group. The label row's own internal gap is a raw 10px rather than a token.
The track and indicator take radius/sm at small and radius/md at medium while Shape is rounded, and radius/none while it is sharp. The radius scales with thickness so the ends stay fully round.

The indicator's width is the value expressed as a share of the 408px track. Figma samples it at 0, 204 and 408px because a variant cannot carry a number, and both Indeterminate and Buffering draw a fixed 143px segment instead.
Buffering adds a 306px band on surface/subtle at 10 percent opacity, between the indicator and the end of the track.
label/medium (14/20), IBM Plex Sans Medium.
The indicator is foreground/link, the track border/subtle and the label foreground/secondary. The buffered band is the only element relying on an opacity rather than a token value alone.
